sources.publicationStatus: Final journal publication; metadata firstPublicationDate 2018-09-19. Version/access details below.

sources.design: Systematic review of three small RCTs, 93 enrolled participants.
sources.population: Mostly women in their 50 s with stage I/II posterior tibial dysfunction/tendinopathy.
sources.comparator: Resistance types plus orthoses/stretching versus orthoses/stretching or no intervention.
sources.coInterventions: Orthoses and stretching limit attribution to strengthening alone.
sources.outcomes: Possible added eccentric benefit, but sparse evidence and poor dose reporting. The moderate home program in Houck showed minimal additional benefit.
sources.uncertainty: Only three small early-stage trials, sparse exercise reporting and multimodal care. Table 3 is an indirect extraction of primary protocols, whose exact apparatus was not independently verified. No generalisation to advanced rigid deformity.
sources.limitations: Only three small early-stage trials, sparse exercise reporting and multimodal care. Table 3 is an indirect extraction of primary protocols, whose exact apparatus was not independently verified. No generalisation to advanced rigid deformity. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: Table 3 describes plantarflexed adduction: concentric neutral to end range or eccentric in reverse. Houck used bilateral/single-leg heel raises and band adduction/inversion in plantarflexion.
protocol.dose: Kulig review table: 3 × 15 at 15 RM, 5-second contraction, 1–2-minute rests. Houck: 2–3 × 10 progressing toward 30. These are indirect trial extractions.
protocol.frequency: Twice daily for 12 weeks in the review table.
protocol.progression: Review table describes load/repetition changes; exact primary apparatus/instructions remain unresolved.
protocol.stoppingRules: not reported as universal stopping rules.

sources.population: Adults with stage I/II posterior tibial tendinopathy.
sources.comparator: Orthoses/stretching versus the same care plus concentric or eccentric progressive resistance.
sources.coInterventions: All groups used orthoses and stretching.
sources.outcomes: FFI improved in all groups; the eccentric group improved most. Pain after the five-minute walk improved across groups.
sources.uncertainty: Small early-stage trial with orthoses/stretching in every arm and no untreated comparator. Full primary exercise protocol and harms not retrieved; review-extracted details must remain attributed to the review.

sources.limitations: Small early-stage trial with orthoses/stretching in every arm and no untreated comparator. Full primary exercise protocol and harms not retrieved; review-extracted details must remain attributed to the review. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

sources.design: Randomised trial of stage II dysfunction; 36 participants in analysed groups according to the review.
sources.population: Middle-aged adults with stage II dysfunction managed with an orthosis.
sources.comparator: Orthosis/stretching versus the same care plus moderate home strengthening.
sources.coInterventions: Orthosis and stretching in both groups.
sources.outcomes: Both groups improved pain/function; between-group differences were minimal. Deep posterior-compartment isometric strength did not differ.
sources.uncertainty: Moderate home strengthening added little to orthosis/stretching. Full primary methods/harms unavailable; trial cannot establish a universally ineffective or harmful exercise.
sources.harms: not reported in the accessible abstract.
sources.limitations: Moderate home strengthening added little to orthosis/stretching. Full primary methods/harms unavailable; trial cannot establish a universally ineffective or harmful exercise. Research candidate only; no clinical release.

protocol.execution: reported in accessible text: Abstract > Methods compares prefabricated orthosis plus stretching with orthosis plus stretching/strengthening. Exact exercise mechanics are not described.
protocol.dose: reported in accessible text: Abstract > Results reports a 12-week trial period, with Methods assessing outcomes six and twelve weeks after exercise began. These are program/assessment intervals, not per-exercise dose or session frequency.
protocol.supervision: reported in accessible text: Abstract > Background and Conclusions identify a moderate-intensity home-based program; direct-supervision arrangements and visit counts are not reported.

findings.statement: Possible added eccentric benefit, but sparse evidence and poor dose reporting. The moderate home program in Houck showed minimal additional benefit. Harms: No reliable pooled harms estimate.
findings.applicability: Mostly women in their 50 s with stage I/II posterior tibial dysfunction/tendinopathy.
findings.limitations: Only three small early-stage trials, sparse exercise reporting and multimodal care. Table 3 is an indirect extraction of primary protocols, whose exact apparatus was not independently verified. No generalisation to advanced rigid deformity.

Houck: 2–3 × 10 progressing toward 30. These are indirect trial extractions. Frequency: Twice daily for 12 weeks in the review table.
